Q: new-to-coding ways to learn for free, language(s) to start with, sources of information, things to avoid, etiquette, etc A:

I agree with learning Python first - it's a fantastic first language. As a beginner you want to be concentrating on the basic code constructs (assignments, conditions, loops) writing algorithms, and above all making progress fast. Python even forces good code layout. If you start with something like Java then where is a whole world of extra thing you have to deal with before you can get your first program to run. This will slow you down and that is demoralising

That said, as soon as you feel comfortable with Python move on to something else (not instead of Python, as well as Python). Apart from the fact having a couple of languages under your belt is no bad thing, there are all the things you skipped by starting to Python (Class structures, data hiding, static methods, command line arguments, compiling and build tools). These are important things in their own right, but they can wait until you are comfortable with algorithms. At this point Java would be a good choice, although the dot-net languages are also worth looking at.

After that I'd recommend adding another, very different language. Practically SQL is probably your best bet, but if you are interested in low-level work then C might be the way to go.

Q: How to solve the INVALID NOTEBOOK (The Notebook Does Not Appear to Be Valid JSON) error on GitHub? A:

I found a more interesting solution here. It actually works for me:

  1. Rename your .ipynb file to .json.
  2. Search for "metadata": { within the JSON file.
  3. Inside the metadata block, look for a "widgets": { ... } section.
  4. Carefully delete the entire "widgets": { ... } block, including the opening and closing curly braces and any content within it.
  5. Save the modified JSON file.
  6. Rename the file back to its original .ipynb extension (e.g., mynotebook.json to mynotebook.ipynb).
